level_1: Obtains history and physical exam to form a patient assessment
level_2: Evaluates patients; orders and interprets diagnostic testing
level_3: Develops a plan to manage patients with straightforward conditions
level_4: Develops a plan to manage patients with complex conditions and adapts plan for changing clinical situation
level_5: Develops a clinical pathway for the management of patients with complex conditions or identifies clinical trials for patients

level_1: Identifies alterations in normal physiology
level_2: Accurately and reliably gathers and reports clinical information pertaining to common peri-procedural alterations and complications
level_3: Independently identifies and prioritizes tasks necessary for management of common peri-procedural alterations and complications
level_4: Independently identifies and prioritizes tasks necessary for management of complex and/or less common peri- procedural alterations and complications
level_5: Proactively recognizes potential risk factors for complications, and implements measures to prevent or mitigate them, applying effective team management skills to manage multiple scenarios simultaneously

level_1: Prepares patient and equipment for endoscopic procedures (e.g., lithotomy positioning, assemble endoscope)
Independently performs complex endoscopic procedures in altered anatomy (e.g., horseshoe kidney, urinary diversion, spinal malformation)
level_2: Independently performs bedside endoscopic procedures (e.g., cystoscopy with catheter placement over a wire)
level_3: Independently performs simple endoscopic procedures (e.g., simple transurethral resection of a bladder tumor (TURBT), simple ureteroscopy (URS), small transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP))
level_4: Independently performs complex endoscopic procedures (e.g., percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL), complex URS, complex TURBT, large
level_5: TURP)

level_1: Demonstrates basic skills (e.g., positioning, knot tying, suturing)
level_2: Independently performs bedside open procedures (e.g., incision and drainage, priapism aspiration and irrigation, circumcision, removal of genital wart)
level_3: Independently performs simple open procedures (e.g., scrotal procedures, vasectomy, cystorrhaphy, mid-urethral sling)
level_4: Independently performs complex open procedures (e.g., partial nephrectomy, prosthetic replacement, cystectomy and ileal conduit, ureteral reconstruction)
level_5: Independently performs uncommon complex open procedures (e.g., retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND), nephrectomy with caval thrombus, reconstructive genital surgery)

level_1: Demonstrates basic skills (e.g., positioning, draping, docking and undocking)
level_2: Assists during minimally invasive procedures (e.g., port placement, bedside assistant)
level_3: Independently performs simple portions of the procedure (e.g., bladder takedown, colon reflection, pelvic lymph node dissection)
level_4: Independently performs critical (complex) portions of the procedure (e.g., hilar dissection, renorrhaphy, anastomosis)
level_5: Independently performs advanced minimally invasive procedures (e.g., cystectomy, complex partial nephrectomy, complex reconstruction)

level_1: Demonstrates basic skills in office procedures (e.g., Foley catheter placement, drain removal)
level_2: Performs simple office- based procedures, with direct supervision (e.g., prostate biopsy, urodynamics interpretation, vasectomy, urethral stricture dilation)
level_3: Independently performs simple office-based procedures, including percutaneous suprapubic tube placemen
level_4: Independently performs complex office-based procedures (e.g., renal ultrasound, bladder biopsy, Botox injection)
level_5: Independently performs advanced office-based procedures (e.g., stage 1 neuromodulation, minimally invasive benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) procedure, penile ultrasound)

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of anatomy and physiology as it pertains to surgical conditions
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of pathophysiology and treatments of simple urologic conditions
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of pathophysiology and treatments of complex urologic conditions considering patient factors (e.g., comorbidity, social context)
level_4: Demonstrates comprehensive knowledge, including guidelines, of the full spectrum of urologic diseases, treatments, and populations
level_5: Creates a curriculum for clinical medical knowledge

level_1: Integrates patient- specific information to generate an appropriate working diagnosis
level_2: Provides a prioritized differential diagnosis using supporting rationale
level_3: Independently synthesizes clinical information to inform diagnosis and therapy in simple cases and adapts based on a patient’s clinical course and additional data
level_4: Independently synthesizes clinical information to inform diagnosis and therapy in complex cases, recognizing sources of error
level_5: Teaches others to recognize sources of diagnostic error

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events and institutional reporting system
Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Offers strategies (simulated or actual) to prevent patient safety events
level_3: Identifies and reports patient safety events
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_4: Describes local quality improvement initiatives (e.g., multimodal analgesics, antibiotic stewardship, smoking cessation, hospital acquired infection)
Actively engages and leads teams and processes to prevent patient safety events
level_5: Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination and community health needs
Supervises safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs of junior residents
level_2: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Leads care coordination of patients with barriers or other disparities in care (e.g., trauma patient with no access to care)
level_3: Coordinates multidisciplinary care of patients in routine clinical situations, considering inequities and disparities for their local population (e.g., cultural barriers)
Resolves conflicts in transitions of care between teams
level_4: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Designs innovative care coordination strategies for populations with health care inequities
level_5: Coordinates multidisciplinary care of patients in complex clinical situation and incorporates local resources into the plan (e.g., home parenteral nutrition, postoperative intravenous feeding, intensive care unit)
Leads in the design and implementation of improvements to transitions of care

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies basic needs for effective transition to practice (e.g., information technology, legal, billing and coding, financial, personnel)
Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system performance (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems (e.g., government, private, public, uninsured care) and practice models
Analyzes individual practice patterns and professional requirements in preparation for practice
level_3: Demonstrates use of information technology required for medical practice (e.g., electronic health record, documentation required for billing and coding)
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care (e.g., patient payment models, insurance)
level_4: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated and how this impacts patient care
Educates others to prepare them for transition to practice
level_5: Describes core administrative knowledge needed for transition to independent practice (e.g., contract negotiations, malpractice insurance, government regulation, compliance)
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care

level_1: Demonstrates how to access available evidence
level_2: Articulates clinical questions to guide evidence-based care
level_3: Integrates best available evidence with patient preferences to guide care
level_4: Tailors patient care in the setting of conflicting or absent evidence
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for patients with complex conditions

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Identifies gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Integrates practice data and feedback with humility to implement a learning plan
level_2: Establishes goals for personal and professional development
Continuously reflects on remaining gaps and institutes behavioral adjustments to narrow them
level_3: Analyzes and reflects on the factors which contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and adapts when necessary
level_4: Identifies opportunities for performance improvement; designs a learning plan
Coaches others on reflective practice
level_5: Institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Coaches others in the design and implementation of learning plans

level_1: Demonstrates professional behavior in routine situations and knows how to report professionalism lapses
Seeks help in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of ethical principles underlying shared decision making and patient confidentiality
Recognizes and intervenes in situations to prevent professionalism lapses in self and others
level_3: Demonstrates insight into personal triggers for professionalism lapses, develops mitigation strategies
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review)
level_4: Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
level_2: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations
level_4: Recognizes situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner and proposes solutions
level_5: Develops systems to enhance other’s ability to efficiently complete administrative tasks and responsibilities

level_1: Recognizes status of personal and professional well-being, with assistance
level_2: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being
level_3: With assistance, proposes a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_4: Independently develops a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
level_5: Coaches others when emotional responses do not meet professional expectations

level_1: Demonstrates respect and establishes rapport with patient and family (e.g., situational awareness of language, disability, health literacy level, cultural)
When prompted, reflects on personal biases while attempting to minimize communication barriers
level_2: Communicates with patients and their families in an understandable and respectful manner
Facilitates difficult discussions specific to patient and family conferences, (e.g., end- of-life, explaining complications, therapeutic uncertainty)
level_3: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters
Independently recognizes personal biases while attempting to proactively minimize communication barriers
level_4: Identifies barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy, cultural)
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection
level_5: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging encounters (e.g., shared decision making)
Coaches others in the facilitation of crucial conversations

subcompetencies.name: Patient Counseling and Shared Decision Making

level_1: Demonstrates basic understanding of informed consent process
level_2: Answers questions about treatment plan and seeks guidance when appropriate
level_3: Counsels patient through decision-making process, including questions, for simple clinical problems
level_4: Counsels patient through decision- making process, including questions, for complex clinical problems
level_5: Counsels patient through decision-making process, including questions, for uncommon clinical problems

level_1: Respectfully interacts and actively communicates with all members of health care team (e.g., politely accepts and requests consults)
level_2: Communicates in an approachable and productive manner to facilitate team work (e.g., active listening updates in timely fashion duality)
level_3: Actively recognizes and mitigates communication barriers and biases with members of the health care team
level_4: Leads and coordinates recommendations from multidisciplinary members of the health care team (e.g., facilitates conflict resolution)
level_5: Exemplar of flexible communication strategies

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record in a timely manner while safeguarding patient personal health information
level_2: Documents diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record with appropriate use of documentation shortcuts
level_3: Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning
level_4: Efficiently communicates in an organized fashion that includes contingency plans
level_5: Facilitates improved written and verbal communication of others
